Mara reached the harbor just before dawn, carrying a letter from the mountain village. The fishing boats were still tied to the pier, and a thin layer of frost covered their ropes. At the warehouse, she found the captain checking a damaged compass. He listened to her account of the blocked road, then spread a map across an empty crate. The eastern trail was shorter, but yesterday's rain had washed away part of its stone wall. They agreed to send supplies by boat and ask the lighthouse keeper to guide the crew through the narrow channel. Mara bought bread for the journey and helped load medicine, blankets, and two sacks of grain. When the tide began to rise, the captain gave each passenger a life jacket and explained where to wait during rough weather. A young carpenter stayed behind to repair the village cart. From the deck, Mara watched him wave until the harbor disappeared into the morning mist. She hoped the letter would reach her sister before the next snowfall.
